Case: Sylvester is a 29-year-old metastatic medulloblastoma status-post multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, presenting with several months of progressive leg pain. Sylvester describes the pain as sometimes crampy and other times sharp, involving different regions of both his legs at different times. In addition to his deconditioning, he is now unable to sleep due to constant pain. On physical examination, you detect diffuse bilateral lower extremity weakness with intact sensation. You obtain a surveillance MRI of his entire spine and discover drop metastases seeding extensive regions of his spinal cord and thecal sac, with multiple lower nerve roots engorged by tumor.
Question: Would you offer morphine to Sylvester? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
